label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
problem_in_my_words: The author could not make slides move, so he talked over his own pictures; a team of agents running a loop let him show the movement and keep changing it until the last hour.
why: The empty chair for security and the promise of nine agents with one job each intrigue me, but the chapter never says what the factory cost, what went wrong, or whether my own team could do this with the one agent each of us already has. It is about a talk and a slide tool, not yet about my stand and my deadline.
my_sentence: I want my team to understand X, and after reading they should be able to do Y. The instruction is clear, but it is about one idea, not our event, and it does not tell me who writes it or where it goes.

by_section.why: The still slide versus the movement is concrete and the voice note is honest. It is a presenter's problem more than mine, but I recognise talking over a picture.
by_section.quote: I talked over my own pictures.

by_section.why: The long animation quote is about users, agents and gold, which means nothing to me yet. I read it as a demo I cannot see, and the line about changing it at 18:26 is the real hook but arrives late.
See, ask, see again is a pattern I can copy with my own agent. The times (13:50, 15:07, 18:25) make it feel real. This is where I start to care.
by_section.quote: That is a feedback loop. See it, ask for it differently, see it again.

by_section.why: A conference talk citation and a concession that the day did not live up to it. Pleasant, but I am a busy person on a phone and it adds no takeaway.
by_section.quote: Creators need an immediate connection to what they create.

by_section.why: This is the section that should define the factory and it is vague: nine agents, one page of rules, a brake, but no picture of who does what or how it stops. The figure of greyed cards is a promise, not an explanation.
by_section.quote: A team of AI agents, gathered around one objective, run hard for one day, and taken apart when the job was done.

by_section.why: Short, doable in a gap between meetings. Weak only because it is about an idea rather than my team's job.
by_section.quote: That sentence is your first brief.

cut: Trim the Bret Victor section to two sentences and shorten the animation quote; spend the room on one concrete line saying what the factory is and how it stops.
best_line: I talked over my own pictures.
worst_moment: The animation quote in Pressing play: a long block describing something I cannot see, about gold and agents, before I know why it matters.
notes: The chapter never says what a reader with their own agent should do on Monday, and the one-central-person worry is untouched: the editor signs and decides everything. A line saying the loop works with a team of people, each with an agent, would answer my deal-breaker early. The two Figure notes are skipped as the reader cannot see them.
